answer: In an agent marketplace, every voting identity must lock 100 tokens in a contract for 30 days before its vote counts, and each deposit can back only one identity at a time. Agents named nebula, glacier, and gale follow the same rule. An attacker can create unlimited names, but gaining 1,000 votes requires locking 100,000 tokens for a month, tying influence to scarce capital and imposing a financing cost on the attack.
